Merges `mngr/linux-packaging` and `mngr/linux-dev-packaging` (see `mngr-linux-packaging.md`, `mngr-linux-dev-packaging.md`, and `mngr-linux-install-fixes.md`):

- `minds-launch-to-msg.yml` gains a `linux_artifacts` job that extracts the build's `.deb` and AppImage on an Ubuntu runner and verifies every bundled tool is a runnable x86-64 ELF, the `.deb` carries `package-type`, and the bundled wheels resolve into a working `minds`; `scripts/release_channel` publishes one manifest per platform an entry lists.

- `ci.yml` (and the public-mirror overlay) gain `test-minds-linux-install`, which runs `apps/minds/scripts/install-linux.sh --yes --no-launch --skip-docker` from the checkout and asserts the pinned toolchain, the Electron dependencies, the bundled git, the UI bundle, the launcher, and `uv run minds run --help`.

- `.github/workflows/mirror-tags.yml` and `scripts/mirror_tag.py` re-point `minds-v*` release tags onto the public mirror.

- The private `just minds-start` and `just minds-start-cloud` recipes end by running `apps/minds/scripts/start-desktop.sh`.

- `scripts/mirror_tag.py` treats a mirror whose newest exported commit is not in the workflow's checkout (main moved after the checkout and the mirror exported it) as caught up, instead of failing the tag on the unknown commit; `scripts/release_channel/publish.py` prints each platform's publish line as its upload completes, so a platform whose upload fails does not hide what was already written.

- `specs/minds-linux-packaging/spec.md` records decision 13: on Ubuntu 24.04 and later the `.deb` relaunches itself without the `--no-sandbox` that ToDesktop's probe launcher passes, because the package's own AppArmor profile already lets the app create the user namespaces Chromium's sandbox needs; the earlier claim that only a ToDesktop change could restore the sandbox was wrong. The same decision records why that relaunch, and the restart after any Linux update, spawn the replacement from the browser process through a detached shell rather than leaving it to electron-updater: its `.deb` updater restarts through `app.relaunch`, whose relauncher hands the replacement `no_new_privs`, under which the next update's `pkexec dpkg -i` cannot run, and its AppImage updater starts the replaced file before the old process has quit, where it dies on the single-instance lock and its arrival raises the window over the running-workspaces prompt. The install policy's `relaunchedBy: 'app'` therefore switches electron-updater's own restart off for every Linux install (`electron/appimage-updater.js` keeps the AppImage updater's file replacement and drops its start), and the quit-time dialogs are owned by the app's most recent window so no raise can hide them.

- `test_meta_ratchets.py`: the two mngr-level vocabulary ratchets were tightened on this branch (workspace vocabulary 337 to 326, minds references 345 to 322) as the branch removed violations; `main` has since added a few of its own, so after merging `main` the snapshots sit at the merged counts, 333 and 324, still below what `main` allows.
